judged_text: Email delivery failure is swallowed by `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` — the error object is discarded and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. When the SMTP/mail provider fails, guests and organizer are never notified yet the user sees the success toast 'Guests added', and the single console.log without the error leaves operators unable to diagnose the lost invites.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). This means the client’s `onSuccess` toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) will fire even if SMTP/provider fails, and operators lose diagnostics because the caught `err` is not logged or surfaced. However, from the diff alone it’s not provable that email delivery must be coupled to mutation success (guests are still added and calendar attendees updated), so this is best treated as an observability/UX consistency issue rather than a guaranteed correctness defect.
